report_metadata.framework_name: AI-Assisted Passive Network Forensic Framework for Email Cryptographic Security Posture Assessment

controls.name: Email Protocol Identification
controls.expected: SMTP, IMAP, or POP3 protocol traffic
controls.why: Email transport and retrieval protocol traffic successfully parsed from network capture.
controls.evidence: Total email sessions identified: 4 across protocols IMAP, POP3, SMTP
controls.recommendation: Maintain continuous network monitoring on standard email ports.

controls.name: STARTTLS / STLS Upgrade Enforcement
controls.observed: Cleartext session(s) without STARTTLS/STLS upgrade (3 session(s))
controls.expected: STARTTLS / STLS Upgrade Enforced on All Cleartext Connections
controls.why: Session initiated in cleartext without requesting or accepting STARTTLS/STLS encryption upgrade.
controls.recommendation: Configure email servers to enforce STARTTLS (SMTP/IMAP) and STLS (POP3) upgrades before handling mail.

controls.name: Plaintext Authentication Protection
controls.observed: No authentication commands transmitted in cleartext
controls.expected: Authentication Commands Restricted to TLS Encrypted Sessions
controls.why: No unencrypted authentication attempts were detected.
controls.evidence: All authentication commands occurred within encrypted TLS sessions.
controls.recommendation: Continue restricting AUTH commands to encrypted channels.

controls.name: TLS Protocol Version Compliance
controls.why: Session negotiated recommended TLS version (TLS 1.2 or TLS 1.3).

controls.name: Cipher Suite Security
controls.why: Negotiated cipher suite meets modern cryptographic standards.

controls.name: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS)
controls.observed: Ephemeral Key Exchange (ECDHE/DHE) Negotiated (3/3 TLS sessions)
controls.why: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) is active, protecting past communications from decryption.
controls.recommendation: Maintain Ephemeral Diffie-Hellman key exchange preference.

controls.name: Elliptic Curve Selection
controls.why: Standardized curves provide performance and resistance against side-channel attacks.

controls.name: Certificate Trust & Authority
controls.expected: Certificate Issued by Recognized Public or Enterprise CA
controls.why: Self-signed certificates cannot be validated by standard public trust stores, introducing trust ambiguity for external mail clients.
controls.evidence: Evidence: Certificate subject 'CN=mail.example.local,OU=Security,O=EmailForensicsTest,L=SanFrancisco,ST=California,C=US' matches issuer.; Certificate subject 'CN=mail.example.local,OU=Security,O=EmailForensicsTest,L=SanFrancisco,ST=California,C=US' matches issuer.; Certificate subject 'CN=mail.example.local,OU=Security,O=EmailForensicsTest,L=SanFrancisco,ST=California,C=US' matches issuer.
controls.recommendation: Deploy certificates issued by a trusted enterprise or public Certificate Authority.

controls.name: Certificate Lifetime & Expiration
controls.observed: Certificate Currently Active & Valid (approximately 360.83 days remaining)
controls.why: Certificate activation timestamp is valid and expiration date is in the future.
controls.evidence: Inspected 3 certificate(s); all within valid lifetime.

controls.name: Certificate Hostname & SNI Alignment
controls.observed: mail.example.local → MATCH (Server SNI Matches Certificate Subject / SAN)
controls.expected: Target Server FQDN Matches Certificate SAN / Subject
controls.why: Target hostname matches certificate subject name.
controls.evidence: Validated hostname match for 3 certificate session(s).
controls.recommendation: Maintain SNI alignment on load balancers and mail servers.

controls.name: Public Key Size Compliance
controls.why: Public key size satisfies modern NIST cryptographic guidelines.

controls.name: Signature Algorithm Security
controls.why: Certificate signature algorithm satisfies modern security baselines.

controls.name: TLS Client / Server Fingerprinting (JA3 / JA4)
controls.observed: NOT AVAILABLE IN CAPTURE (Optional Zeek Fingerprint Package Not Installed)
controls.expected: JA3 / JA3S / JA4 Fingerprint String for Client/Server Profiling
controls.why: JA3 and JA4 fingerprinting require optional Zeek package extensions which were not active during capture logging.
controls.evidence: Fields ja3: null, ja3s: null, ja4: null, ja4s: null across all captured sessions.
controls.recommendation: If client fingerprinting is required, install zeek-ja3 or zeek-ja4 packages in the Zeek deployment.

findings.title: Cleartext IMAP Session
findings.description: IMAP session established on port 143 without STARTTLS or implicit TLS.
findings.evidence: IMAP session on port 143 transmitted in cleartext without STARTTLS/STLS upgrade.
findings.security_impact: Mailbox contents and user authentication credentials are exposed to passive eavesdropping.
references: RFC 8314 (Use of TLS for Email Submission and Access)
findings.recommendation: Disable plaintext port 143 or enforce STARTTLS / implicit TLS on port 993.
findings.technical_remediation: Disable plaintext port 143 or enforce STARTTLS / implicit TLS on port 993.

findings.title: Cleartext POP3 Session
findings.description: POP3 session established on port 110 without STLS or implicit TLS.
findings.evidence: POP3 session on port 110 transmitted in cleartext without STARTTLS/STLS upgrade.
findings.security_impact: Email downloads and user credentials transmitted unencrypted.
references: RFC 8314 (Use of TLS for Email Submission and Access)
findings.recommendation: Disable plaintext port 110 or enforce STLS / implicit TLS on port 995.
findings.technical_remediation: Disable plaintext port 110 or enforce STLS / implicit TLS on port 995.

findings.title: Cleartext SMTP Connection without STARTTLS
findings.description: The SMTP session was established over plain TCP on port 25 or 587 without negotiating STARTTLS encryption.
findings.evidence: SMTP session on port 25 transmitted in cleartext without STARTTLS/STLS upgrade.
findings.security_impact: Eavesdroppers and active network adversaries can read, modify, or inject email messages, credentials, and headers in transit.
references: RFC 7590 (Use of TLS in Email Applications)
NIST SP 800-45 Rev 2 (Guidelines on Electronic Mail Security)
findings.recommendation: Reconfigure SMTP MTA (PostFix, Exim, Sendmail) to mandate STARTTLS: `smtpd_tls_security_level = encrypt`.
findings.technical_remediation: Reconfigure SMTP MTA (PostFix, Exim, Sendmail) to mandate STARTTLS: `smtpd_tls_security_level = encrypt`.

findings.title: Self-Signed Certificate in Use
findings.description: Server certificate subject matches issuer and is not signed by a trusted Certificate Authority.
findings.security_impact: Clients cannot verify server identity, exposing connections to Man-in-the-Middle (MITM) spoofing.
findings.recommendation: Replace self-signed certificate with an X.509 certificate issued by a trusted public CA (e.g. Let's Encrypt) or internal enterprise PKI.
findings.technical_remediation: Replace self-signed certificate with an X.509 certificate issued by a trusted public CA (e.g. Let's Encrypt) or internal enterprise PKI.
